# `check.waive`

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs-gen` from crates/ew-commands/schemas/check.waive.schema.json. Do not edit: change the source and regenerate. -->

`check.waive` (`WaiveFinding`): records a waiver that accepts one finding (doc 15 §2.5, FR-CHK-009; WP-S1.16 D7,
FT-494): `Waiver {rule, target: {finding}, reason, author, date}` with a new ID.

The finding is named by its rule ID and its fingerprint (32 hex digits, FR-CHK-044; stored in lower case). The
author (the display name the GUI records) and the date are parameters: the command reads no clock and no
operating-system user (WP-S1.16 §10 rule 2). The check engine then reports the matching finding as waived; a
waiver that matches no finding stays and is reported (EW-CORE-081), and a rule whose findings cannot be waived
(an integrity or system rule) gives no waived finding either.

Rejected: a rule ID that is not of the form `EW-<PACK>-<three digits>` (at `/rule`); a fingerprint that is not 32
hex digits (at `/fingerprint`); an empty reason or one with a text shorter than `WAIVER_REASON_MIN_CHARS`
characters (at `/reason`); a finding that a waiver of the same rule covers already (the existing waiver is named).

**Exposure `HumanOnly`** (ADR-0019 decision 8, doc 15 §2.5 "Who may waive"): a scripted waiver would defeat the
record, so command logs, scripts, MCP and plugins get `CmdError::Exposure`. Interactive; undoable as one step.
Outcome: the waiver.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `author` | [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident) | yes |  | The author's display name. |
| `date` | [`Date`](#date) | yes |  | The date of the waiver. |
| `fingerprint` | string | yes |  | The finding's fingerprint, 32 hex digits. |
| `reason` | [`CmdMlText`](#cmdmltext) | yes |  | Why the finding is accepted: at least ten characters in every language given. |
| `rule` | [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident) | yes |  | The rule ID of the finding (`EW-CORE-041`). |

## Types

### CmdIdent

An identifier: non-empty, one line, NFC, without leading or trailing white space (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 1 character(s))

Pattern: `^[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000](?:[^\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]*[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000])?$`

### CmdMlText

Multilingual text: a neutral string, or an object keyed by canonical BCP 47 tags in ascending order with non-empty string values (doc 05 §3.2).

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**

   Shape: string

2. **Form 2**

   Shape: map of string (at least 1 character(s)) (at least 1 propert(ies))

### Date

An authored date YYYY-MM-DD (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`)

Pattern: `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`

## Exit codes

A command runs as one line of a command log replayed by `ew apply` ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)). The exit code of `ew apply` is:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The line committed as one transaction. |
| 1 | A prevent rule or the command's own domain rule refused the line (`Prevented`, `Rejected`); without `--one-step` the lines before it stay committed and are saved, with `--one-step` nothing is saved. |
| 2 | Anything else stops the replay: invalid parameters, a missing record, an unresolvable reference, an open, lock or save error. |

The codes of every subcommand are in [doc 17 §3.2](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#32-exit-codes).

Exposure class `human_only`: [doc 17 §2.3](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#23-origins-and-exposure-classes) says whether a command log may run it.
